correctness.rationale: The involution covers t->1/t, so its fixed points can occur only over t=±1. The original Proposition4.13 bad-fiber polynomial is nonzero at both values. At t=1 the affine action is (x,y)->(x,-y), yielding four simple F_1(x)=0 roots; its two weighted-projective infinity points are exchanged. At t=-1 the action is (x,y)->(-x-248+108 sqrt5,y), yielding x=-124+54 sqrt5 and two y choices from the nonzero value 3567475528-1595423560 sqrt5. The weighted-projective infinity points [1:±i:0] are individually fixed (scaling X by -1 preserves Y because of weight 2), giving two more. Thus exactly four fixed points on each smooth fiber and four quotient nodes over each of s=0 and s=-4. The full quartic specialization, separability, smooth-fiber polynomial and affine fixed-value were independently recomputed by exact Q(sqrt5) arithmetic; finite substitution supports exhaustive fixed-locus geometry, which uses base inversion and compactification.
residual_risks: Only this specific Nikulin involution and chosen genus-one quartic, over C.
At infinity the weighted-projective equivalence, not ordinary projective scaling, is essential.
